links.comparator_used: Fully automated AI clinical algorithm development (F-ACAD) without human expert review, benchmarked in a single illustrative run
links.outcome: Safety and clinical quality of the AI-drafted febrile seizure algorithm, plus turnaround time
links.effect: S-ACAD with expert oversight took about 245 min. Two external specialists found no medically inaccurate sections or critical safety errors and rated clinical validity 9.0 and 9.5 out of 10. F-ACAD took about 68 min, and its own AI critics identified 17 issues (9 high-priority). The comparison is descriptive, from a single execution with one expert and one topic.
links.tradeoff: The expert-in-the-loop workflow was much slower (about 245 vs 68 min) and needed 19 recorded human expert interventions.
links.quote: By comparison, the fully automated approach (F-ACAD) completed the task in approximately 68 minutes, but its own AI critics identified 17 issues (9 high-priority), including concerns related to emergency response clarity and standard-of-care alignment.

design_hint: human-in-the-loop expert review vs fully automated generation
